original_question: Prove or disprove that the non-analytic growth bound ζ(T ) of a C0 -semigroup T coincides with the critical growth bound ωcrit (T ).
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 13 (Growth bounds), which asks whether the non-analytic growth bound and the critical growth bound coincide for a C0-semigroup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost exactly: it uses the correct two quantities, asks for equality, and phrases the task as a prove-or-disprove problem for a C0-semigroup T. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
missing_details: Add the universal quantifier explicitly: the paper poses the question for an arbitrary C0-semigroup, i.e. for every T=(T(t))_{t≥0}.
State the ambient setting: the paper’s global scope is C0-semigroups of bounded linear operators on Banach spaces.

Make explicit that no additional hypotheses are assumed in the general problem; the nearby comments mention Hilbert-space semigroups, Banach-space semigroups with an L^p-resolvent, and eventually differentiable semigroups only as already understood special cases.
For full stand-alone readability, identify ζ(T) and ω_crit(T) as the standard non-analytic growth bound and critical growth bound of T.
refined_question: For every C0-semigroup T=(T(t))_{t≥0} on a Banach space X, does one have ζ(T)=ω_crit(T), where ζ(T) is the non-analytic growth bound of T and ω_crit(T) is the critical growth bound of T?
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful rewrite because the exact official target in the paper is Section 3, Problem 13, and the abstract fixes the paper’s ambient framework as C0-semigroups on Banach spaces. The nearby comments show that Hilbert-space structure, an L^p-resolvent, and eventual differentiability are special positive cases rather than part of the general hypothesis.
